title: test-results
description: The tester stage's structured record of the validation it authored. The stage executes no test command: on a target whose suite outlasts an agent's per-call ceiling that run cannot complete inside one turn, so the coordinator runs the configured test_command as a subprocess after the turn ends and records the result in suite-run-result.json. WHAT A READER LOSES AND WHY IT IS NOT REPLACED: this artifact used to carry status, tests_run, tests_passed, tests_failed and failures, so a reader could see a pass or a failure count without opening another file. Those fields existed only because the stage parsed its own suite output, and any contract requiring them is a contract on the target's test framework — the assumption the harness removed from its source when it stopped naming a language or a runner. Moving that parsing into a prompt would not be removing it, so the counts are removed rather than reproduced. What replaces the verdict is stronger than what it replaces: an exit code from a subprocess the coordinator owns, in suite-run-result.json, beside the path to the run's whole output. What is left here is what the author knows without running anything.

tests_written.description: Number of new tests this stage authored. A fact about what was written, which is what this stage does, rather than about what running them produced.
